as is said,
four hundred cities.
Möngke Khan was compelled to gather a very large army,
and go in person to confront that Chinese king.
And taking with him his brother Kublai, who was younger than he,
he went to the country of the inner Chinese.
And he left in his place his brother Ariq Böke,
who was the youngest of them.
And when he went and confronted that king,
by an evil chance an arrow struck him,
and there he died.
And his brother Kublai led all the forces of the Mongols,
and departed from the inner country of the Chinese,
and settled in their outer country,
in the great city called Khanbaliq.
And the nobles agreed that he should be Khan.
His younger brother, Ariq
Böke, however, said,
"To me belongs the kingdom,
because Möngke Khan committed it to me when he went to war,
and during his lifetime he seated me in his place."
And a great dispute arose between the two brothers, and many battles for a period of seventeen years,
until that younger brother was defeated and captured,
and his name perished.
And the kingdom remained exclusively to Kublai Khan, a just and wise king,
a lover of the Christians,
and one who honored the scribes, scholars, and physicians of all nations.
Now Qutuz, after killing Kitbuqa,
took control of Damascus, Aleppo, and all Syria,
and established in every city a governor and magistrates.
And he set out to enter Egypt,
and to prepare forces,
and go out again to meet the whole army of the Tatars.
And on that very journey, when he reached the vicinity of Gaza,
Baibars rose against him—
who was Bunduqdar the Younger, the slave of Bunduqdar the Elder—and killed him.
And he entered Egypt and took control of it,
and was called al-Malik al-Zahir Rukn al-Din.
And at that time the lord of Sinjar fled to him,
who was Ala al-Din, son of Badr al-Din, the lord of Mosul;
and he gave him Aleppo.
And from Bunduqdar great affliction did the Christians of the seacoast suffer and still suffer to this day.
For he ruled over... [marginal note / footnote, OCR?]
the royal city,
Peking of the Chinese or Chincheos.
